title: Progressive Lenses
short: One pair for distance, computer and reading — no visible line.
meta: Progressive (no-line multifocal) lenses fitted in Garden Grove. Measured by our opticians, made with Varilux, ZEISS and HOYA designs. Most vision plans accepted.
lead: Progressive lenses let you see far, at arm's length and up close through one pair of glasses, without the visible line of old-style bifocals. How comfortable they feel depends less on the brand name and more on how precisely they are measured and fitted — which is the part we take personally.
offer: Precise pupil distance and fitting-height measurements taken in the frame you choose
Standard, premium and wide-corridor designs (Essilor Varilux, ZEISS, HOYA)
Computer / office progressives for long days at a screen
Thinner high-index materials for stronger prescriptions
Free follow-up adjustments while you get used to them
honest: Most people adapt to progressives within one to two weeks. If you still struggle after that, come back — a small change to the frame fit often solves it, and we will check the measurements again before anything else.

faqs.q: How long does it take to get progressive lenses?
faqs.a: Many progressives are finished in our in-store lab in about 3 business days. Some premium designs are made by the lens manufacturer and can take longer; we give you the expected date when you order.

faqs.q: Can I use my vision insurance for progressives?
faqs.a: Usually yes. Most vision plans cover a standard progressive and apply a set amount toward premium designs. Bring your insurance information and we will show you exactly what is covered before you decide.

faqs.q: Do I need a new prescription?
faqs.a: You need a current prescription that includes an ADD (reading) power. Prescriptions from any eye doctor are welcome.

title: Blue Light & Transitions Lenses
h1: Blue light filtering and light-adaptive lenses
short: Screen-friendly coatings and lenses that darken in the sun.
meta: Blue light filtering and Transitions light-adaptive lenses in Garden Grove. Anti-glare coatings, photochromic lenses and honest advice on what each one does.
lead: Lens options can be confusing. We explain what each one actually does so you only pay for what helps your day — whether that is less glare at the computer, lenses that darken outdoors, or both.
offer: Blue light filtering coatings and lens materials
Transitions and other light-adaptive (photochromic) lenses in grey, brown and style colors
Premium anti-glare coatings such as Crizal for night driving and screens
Scratch-resistant and easy-clean coatings
Combinations for single vision, progressives and reading glasses
honest: Blue light filters can make screens feel more comfortable for some people, but the American Academy of Ophthalmology does not consider them necessary for eye health. We'll tell you straight whether an anti-glare coating alone would do the job. Also note that most light-adaptive lenses darken less inside a car, because windshields block much of the UV that triggers them.

faqs.q: Are blue light glasses worth it?
faqs.a: They are a comfort choice, not a medical one. If you spend long hours at screens and like how they feel, they are a reasonable option. A good anti-glare coating is often just as helpful.

faqs.q: Can I add Transitions to progressive lenses?
faqs.a: Yes. Light-adaptive options are available for most single vision and progressive lens designs.

faqs.q: Do Transitions lenses work in the car?
faqs.a: Most darken only partly behind a windshield. If you drive a lot in bright sun, we'll show you options designed for that, or prescription sunglasses.

title: Prescription Sunglasses
short: Polarized and tinted lenses made to your prescription.
meta: Prescription sunglasses in Garden Grove — polarized, tinted and mirrored lenses in Ray-Ban, Oakley, Maui Jim, Costa and more. Progressive sunglasses available.
lead: Southern California sun is bright year-round. Prescription sunglasses let you see clearly outdoors without juggling contacts and store-bought shades.
offer: Polarized lenses to cut glare from roads, water and windshields
Solid and gradient tints, mirror finishes
Single vision and progressive sunglasses
Sun frames from brands such as Ray-Ban, Oakley, Maui Jim and Costa
Prescription lenses for many sunglasses you already own (frame permitting)
honest: Strongly curved (wraparound) sport frames can't hold every prescription. We check your prescription against the frame before you order so there are no surprises.

faqs.q: Does vision insurance cover prescription sunglasses?
faqs.a: Some plans do, often as your frame and lens benefit instead of clear glasses. Others offer a discount on a second pair. We'll check your plan for you.

faqs.q: Polarized or regular tint?
faqs.a: Polarized lenses reduce reflected glare and are great for driving and the beach. They can make some phone and dashboard screens look dim, so we'll let you try both.

faqs.q: Can you put my prescription in my own sunglasses?
faqs.a: Often yes, if the frame is in good condition and its curve suits your prescription. See our lens replacement page for details.

title: Contact Lenses
short: Daily, monthly, toric and multifocal lenses from your current prescription.
meta: Buy contact lenses in Garden Grove — daily, bi-weekly, monthly, toric (astigmatism) and multifocal lenses. Bring a current contact lens prescription. Vision plans accepted.
lead: Pick up your contact lenses where you get your glasses. We carry popular daily, bi-weekly and monthly lenses and can order toric lenses for astigmatism and multifocals for reading.
offer: Daily disposable, bi-weekly and monthly lenses
Toric lenses for astigmatism
Multifocal lenses
Annual supplies — often the best value with rebates and insurance
Solutions and lens cases
honest: By federal law we need a valid contact lens prescription, which is different from a glasses prescription — it lists the exact lens brand, curve and diameter. It comes from a contact lens exam and fitting by an eye doctor. If yours has expired, you'll need a new exam first.

faqs.q: Can I buy contacts with my glasses prescription?
faqs.a: No. Contact lenses need their own prescription from a contact lens fitting. We're happy to fill a current contact lens prescription from any eye doctor.

faqs.q: Does my vision insurance cover contacts?
faqs.a: Most plans give a contact lens allowance in place of glasses for that benefit period. We'll check which option gives you more value.

faqs.q: Do you keep lenses in stock?
faqs.a: We keep popular lenses on hand and order the rest. Most orders arrive within a few business days.

title: Kids' Glasses & Myopia Control
h1: Kids' glasses and myopia control in Garden Grove
short: Myopia control lenses and MiSight® contact lenses for nearsighted kids.
meta: Kids' glasses and myopia control in Garden Grove — myopia control spectacle lenses and MiSight® 1 day contact lenses for nearsighted children. Vision plans accepted.
lead: More children are becoming nearsighted, and at younger ages. Along with durable, comfortable glasses, we offer lenses designed to help slow how quickly a child's nearsightedness (myopia) gets worse.
offer: Myopia control spectacle lenses, designed to help slow the progression of nearsightedness in children
MiSight® 1 day contact lenses — daily disposable lenses for myopia control in children
Impact-resistant lens materials for active kids
Careful fitting and free adjustments as they grow
honest: Myopia control lenses and MiSight® are prescribed by an eye doctor, who decides whether they are right for your child and monitors progress at regular check-ups. They are designed to slow myopia, not to reverse it, and results vary from child to child. They work best when worn consistently, every day.

faqs.q: What is myopia control?
faqs.a: Myopia control uses specially designed glasses or contact lenses to help slow how quickly a child's nearsightedness gets worse as they grow. Regular glasses correct blurry vision but are not designed to slow progression.

faqs.q: What is MiSight® 1 day?
faqs.a: MiSight® 1 day is a daily disposable soft contact lens made for myopia control in children. It requires a prescription and fitting from an eye doctor; we can supply it with a valid prescription.

faqs.q: Does insurance cover myopia control lenses?
faqs.a: Coverage varies by plan, and many plans treat myopia control as an upgrade. Call with your plan details and we'll check what's covered before you decide.

title: Sports Goggles
short: Protective eyewear with your prescription for basketball, racquet sports and more.
meta: Prescription sports goggles and protective eyewear in Garden Grove for basketball, soccer, pickleball, racquetball and swimming. Kids and adult sizes.
lead: Regular glasses aren't made for a ball to the face. Prescription sports goggles protect your eyes and keep your vision sharp while you play.
offer: Prescription goggles for basketball, soccer, racquet sports and pickleball
Impact-resistant polycarbonate lenses
Kids' and adult sizes with adjustable straps
Prescription swim goggles (availability depends on prescription)
Sport sunglasses for cycling, running and golf
honest: Street glasses and sunglasses are not rated for sports impact — even with polycarbonate lenses, the frame itself can break. For ball and racquet sports, purpose-made goggles are the safer choice.

faqs.q: Which sports need protective goggles?
faqs.a: Any sport with a fast ball, racquet, stick or elbows nearby — basketball, racquetball, squash, pickleball, soccer and baseball are common examples.

faqs.q: Can goggles hold a strong prescription?
faqs.a: Most prescriptions work. Very strong prescriptions or high astigmatism can limit frame choices; we'll check before you order.

faqs.q: Does insurance cover sports goggles?
faqs.a: Some plans allow them as your frame benefit or offer a discount. We'll check your plan.

title: Lens Replacement in Your Frame
h1: New lenses in your own frame
short: Love your frame? Keep it — we'll put new lenses in it, even if you bought it elsewhere.
meta: Lens replacement in your existing frame in Garden Grove — new prescription lenses for glasses and sunglasses bought anywhere. Most jobs done in our in-store lab.
lead: If you already love your frame, there's no need to buy a new one. Bring it in — even if it came from another store or online — and we'll fit new prescription lenses.
offer: New prescription lenses in frames bought anywhere
Upgrade to progressives, blue light filtering or light-adaptive lenses
Turn a favorite frame into prescription sunglasses
Lenses cut and fitted in our in-store lab
Frame inspection before we start
honest: Every frame is inspected first. Older frames, especially rimless and thin metal ones, can be weakened by age, and there is a small risk that they break during lens fitting. We'll point out any concerns before you decide.

faqs.q: Can you replace lenses in frames I bought online?
faqs.a: Usually yes, as long as the frame is in good condition and suits your prescription.

faqs.q: How long does lens replacement take?
faqs.a: Most jobs are ready in about 3 business days. You may need to leave the frame with us while the lenses are made, so bring a backup pair if you have one.

faqs.q: Will my insurance cover lenses only?
faqs.a: Most vision plans cover lenses separately from frames, so yes in most cases.
